definition: Set of technologies dedicated to designing, programming, and using robots to automate tasks, improve precision, safety, and efficiency in industrial processes.
Techniques for manufacturing and assembling product parts or components using varied methods (welding, bonding, machining, etc.) to ensure quality, reliability, and performance of finished products.
Production method creating objects by adding material layer-by-layer from a 3D digital model, enabling complex, customized parts with less waste than traditional processes.
Real-time surveillance of industrial processes using sensors and data acquisition systems combined with analytical tools to detect anomalies, predict failures, and optimize performance.

Design approach integrating environmental impacts from the earliest stages of product/service development to reduce ecological footprint throughout its lifecycle (raw material extraction to recycling).

sub_domain: Reduction and Treatment of Effluents and Waste
definition: Methods to reduce liquid, solid, or gaseous discharges from industrial activities and treat them to limit environmental and human health impacts.
Practices extending the lifespan of materials/components/products through transformation, repair, or reuse, aligning with circular economy and waste reduction principles.
Manufacturing/transformation techniques minimizing energy consumption, raw material use, and pollutant emissions while promoting renewable/recycled resources.
Transition to low-greenhouse-gas transport modes (land, air, maritime) via electrification, alternative fuels, or energy optimization of vehicles/infrastructure.
Reduction of CO2 emissions from energy production/consumption through renewable energy development, energy efficiency improvements, and fossil fuel substitution.
Development/use of innovative materials (composites, bio-based, nanomaterials) with specific properties (lightness, strength, durability) meeting industrial performance/sustainability demands.
Transformation of industrial activities by integrating digital technologies (IoT, big data, AI, cyber-physical systems) to optimize production, maintenance, quality, and traceability.

sub_domain: Digital Engineering of Products and Processes
definition: Use of digital tools (CAD, simulation, digital twins) to design, model, test, and improve products and manufacturing processes from conception to production.

A company's ability to achieve quality, cost, time, flexibility, and innovation goals through coordinated continuous improvement methods, indicator-based management, integrated digital tools (e.g., ERP), and optimized processes/resources in complex industrial environments.

sub_domain: Preparation for New Jobs in the Future Industry
definition: Actions/training systems to support skill evolution for Industry 4.0, including anticipating competency needs, transforming training pathways, and adapting to emerging technologies (AI, robotics, data).
Process supporting individuals/teams/organizations in transitioning to new practices/tools/models, reducing resistance, facilitating adoption of changes, and ensuring sustainable integration.
Design approach placing end-user needs/expectations/constraints at the core of development, ensuring ergonomics, usability, and satisfaction through deep usage understanding.

sub_domain: Augmentation of Human Capabilities in Manufacturing
definition: Integration of technologies (augmented reality, cobots, AI) to support/amplify operators' physical, cognitive, or decision-making abilities, improving performance/safety/quality while keeping humans central to production.
